DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION NO. 117 s. 2021 Oct. 4, 2021 Hon. REYNALDO GUECO Punong Barangay Malabanias, Angeles City Dear PB Gueco: This refers to your Letter dated 7 August 2021 requesting this Department's legal opinion regarding the irregular actions of Sangguniang Barangay Member Amado Lalic which includes replacing all key personnel in the Barangay during his preventive suspension. As culled from your letter, you were preventively suspended by the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) of Angeles City for ninety (90) days for an alleged violation of health protocols when you held your State of Barangay Address as some of the attendees in the said event were not wearing facemasks. During your suspension period, Mayor Carmelo G. Lazatin, Jr. sworn into office Sangguniang Barangay Amado G. Lalic who is apparently his political ally as the Acting Punong Barangay (PB). Thereafter, Acting PB Lalic removed all key personnel of the barangay, i.e purok leaders, staff and employees and replaced them with his own people through a Barangay Resolution, effectively dissolving the positions and employees. It is also intimated in your letter that salaries of Sangguniang Barangay members and Barangay Personnel services were not paid off. It is your view that while you were serving your preventive suspension, Acting PB Lilac has no authority to declare vacant any position or replace existing personnel. Ostensibly, since you assumed office after having served the ninety (90) days preventive suspension, you were tasked to re-apply for your security bond which you had complied with. However, you were requested to secure a Certificate of No Pending Case from the SP who are apparently all ally of Mayor Lazatin but the SP deprived you to avail the said certification on the premise that the case is still pending. Under such premise, you are requesting from this Department for a clear directive asking herein concemed SP to issue the clearance so that you can effectively exercise and discharge your functions. Foremost, insofar as your view that Sangguniang Barangay Member Lilac, in his capacity as Acting PB, is bereft of authority to replace existing personnel, this Department views otherwise. Assuming arguendo that Sangguniang Barangay Member Lilac is the first ranking Sangguning Barangay Member of Malabanias and his Acting as PB thereat was by operation of law pursuant to Section 46 of the Local Government Code of 1991 , this Department is of the opinion that Sangguniang Barangay member Lilac, in his capacity as Acting PB, is not totally bereft of authority to appoint employees which effectively replace existing personnel in the herein concerned barangay. Section 46 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160, hereinafter referred to as the "Code") provides, thus: Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

"Section 46. Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive. (a) When the governor, city or municipal mayor, or punong barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice-governor, city or municipal vice-mayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. (b) Said temporary incapacity shall terminate upon submission to the appropriate sanggunian of a written declaration by the local chief executive concerned that he has reported back to office. In cases where the temporary incapacity is due to legal causes, the local chief executive concerned shall also submit necessary documents showing that said legal causes no longer exist. From the afore-quoted provision of the Code, it is clear that the Acting Punong Barangay may exercise the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees if the period of temporary incapacity in the office of the incumbent Punong Barangay exceeds thirty (30) working days. In the herein case, you were preventively suspended for longer than thirty (30) days, as such the act of Acting PB Lilac in appointing employees which effectively replaces the existing personnel in the herein concerned barangay does not fall under the prohibition as contemplated in the aforecited provision. However, there is an important condition and caveat here, such that in appointing new barangay officials and employees in replacement of the previous ones, the latter should have been effectively removed first in accordance with the Local Government Code in order to create a vacancy in office. Once vacancies have existed, the Acting PB can now appoint new officials and employees replacing the previous ones. We emphasize that in both removal and appointment, the law provides for the need for concurrence on the part of the majority of all the members of the Sangguniang Barangay to make them valid. Moreover, the removal has to be anchored on a just cause. Acting PB Lilac cannot just remove employees and subsequently replace them sans valid and just cause. Insofar as the appointment or replacement of appointive barangay officials is concerned, Section 389 of the Code provides, thus: "Section 389. Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, and Functions. — (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance, the purpose of which is the general welfare of the barangay and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the punong barangay shall: Xxx (5) Upon approval by a majority of all the members of the sangguniang barangay, appoint or replace the barangay treasurer, the barangay secretary, and other appointive barangay officials. Xxx." (Emphasis supplied) The Supreme Court, in the case of Alquizola et. Vs. Ocol et. al. [G.R. No. 132413, dated 27 August 19991, had explained the above-cited provision of the Code, thus: Page 2 of 5

"The term "replace" would obviously embrace not only the appointment of the replacement but also the prior removal of, or the vacation by, the official currently occupying the appointive position concerned. "To replace" is to take the place of, to serve as a substitute for or successor of, to put in place of, or to fill the post of an incumbent. 1 In order to provide a replacement to an office, the prior holder must have first been removed or the office must have, otherwise, been previously rendered vacant. Aside from what may be implicit in Section 389, there is no other provision in the Local Government Code that treats of the power of the Punong Barangay to remove the barangay secretary, the barangay treasurer, or any other appointive barangay official from office. The duration of the term of office of these barangay officials have not been fixed by the Local Government Code. Where the tenure of the office is not fixed by law, it is a sound and useful rule to consider the power of removal as being an incident to the power of appointment. Elsewise stated, the power to remove is deemed implied in the power to appoint. The Code explicitly vests on the punong barangay, upon approval by a majority of all the members of the sangguniang barangay, the power to appoint or replace the barangay treasurer, the barangay secretary, and other appointive barangay officials. This provision is reinforced, in the case of the secretary and the treasurer, by the provisions of Section 394 and Section 395 of the Local Government Code; to wit: Sec. 394. Barangay Secretary: Appointment, Qualifications, Powers and . — (a) The barangay secretary shall be appointed by the punong Duties barangay with the concurrence of the majority of all the sangguniang barangay members. The appointment of the barangay secretary shall not be subject to attestation by the Civil Service Commission. Sec. 395. Barangay Treasurer: Appointment, Qualifications, Powers and • . — (a) The barangay treasurer shall be appointed by the punong Duties barangay with the concurrence of the majority of all the sangguniang barangay members. The appointment of the barangay treasurer shall not be subject to attestation by the Civil Service Commission. Verily, the power of appointment is to be exercised conjointly by the punong barangay and a majority of all the members of the sangguniang barangay. Without such conjoint action, neither an appointment nor a replacement can be effectual. Applying the rule that the power to appoint includes the power to remove, one that the Court finds no cogent reason to now depart from, the questioned dismissal from office of the barangay officials by the punong barangay without the concurrence of the majority of all the members of the Sangguniang Barangay cannot be legally justified. To rule otherwise could also create an absurd situation of the Sangguniang Barangay members refusing, like here, to give their approval to the replacements selected by the punong barangay who has unilaterally terminated the services of the incumbents. It is likely that the legislature did not intend this absurdity to flow from its enactment of the law." The foregoing pronouncement of the Supreme Court is instructive. It bears to stress, however, that while punong barangays, or in the herein case, acting punong barangay pursuant to Section 46 of the Code, can remove any of the appointed barangay Page 3 of 5

appointive officials, including the barangay treasurer and the barangay secretary, the same should be approved by the majority of all members of the Sangguniang barangay. Under pain of being declared a nullity, majority vote should refer to all the members of the sanggunian. Going now to your request for this Department for a clear directive asking herein concerned SP to issue clearance or a certificate of no pending case, this Department submits that such clearance is not a condition precedent for you to resume your post as PB of Malabanias. The Code did not categorically require that a certificate of no pending case, as what is required by herein concerned SP, be submitted upon the resumption or lifting of suspension decreed by it against a local chief executive after the latter has completely served his suspension. To bolster such view, attention is invited to Section 46 (b) of the Local Government Code, viz: "Section 46. Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive. — (b) Said temporary incapacity shall terminate upon submission to the appropriate sanggunian of a written declaration by the local chief executive concerned that he has reported back to office. In cases where the temporary incapacity is due to legal causes, the local chief executive concerned shall also submit necessary documents showing that said legal causes no longer exist." Accordingly, this Department submits that once the suspension is lifted, the concerned local chief executive may assume his office sans certification from SP as long as a document showing that the legal cause no longer exist. In the herein case, this Department opines that the certification issued by DILG Region Ill, as attached, is sufficient to comply with the above-quoted provision of the Code. Fair play would dictate that after completely serving your 90-day suspension ordered by the SP, you should now be allowed to reassume your post. Even granting arguendo, that a certificate of no pending case is required by law, it is incumbent upon herein concerned SP to issue such certificate to you after the latter has completely served your suspension. Otherwise. failure of SP to qrant such certificate mav warrant for the filinq of an administrative case for dereliction or neqlect of duty before the proper forum. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. ry truly yours, By the Authority of the Secreta B. DINO MA ndersecretary for Barangay Affairs OUSBNMBD/LLLS-LRALLD/jam Page 4 of 5
